exposure: gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) diagnosis during the third trimester
cohort: 238 women who underwent a 50-g glucose challenge test (GCT) with results < 140 mg/dL at 24-28 weeks of gestation and subsequently underwent a 75-g OGTT after 29 weeks of gestation
finding: A diagnosis of GDM during the third trimester did not improve pregnancy outcomes but was associated with an increased rate of elective caesarean delivery.
mod_finding: While a gestational diabetes diagnosis in the third trimester did not impact pregnancy outcomes, it was associated with an increased rate of elective cesarean deliveries.
